summary: Interpreted the impact receipt (a38d65ea01ee4e2ea53193c166144cdd, exit 0, both cases passed) and corrected my earlier account with it: the duplicate TimeoutNow again raised the term (3 -> 4) with the same node re-elected, one sample in 140 showed no leader, and the client write issued at the moment of the duplicate was rejected with 'node is not the leader' — which supersedes the local construction feedback I had reported, where that write still succeeded. The transferred-question account is therefore recorded as explained / defect_claim asserted with both receipts cited: the control message is non-idempotent and carries no context for rejecting a duplicate or stale copy, so a replay forces an extra election whose measured cost includes a short interval in which the node that was leader refuses client work; safety is unaffected because the vote's log-completeness test still guards the replay, and the leader identity did not change in this configuration. Because one write cannot bound that refusal interval, the duplicate case now attempts a write on every 10 ms sampling step and records attempts, rejections, first and last rejection offsets and the window, with one new comparison for a refused client write; local runs of the extension show one rejection out of 137 attempts at the first step and none afterwards. Still open: the quantified refusal-window receipt, delayed rather than duplicated delivery, partitions during replay, larger clusters and interaction with in-flight writes.
